messages:
maria: rolling v5.2.0 to canary (10%) at 08:00 UTC — seeing p99 jump for /v1/generate from ~140ms -> ~420ms in canary cohort. not in control. escalating.

liam: on it. can you paste cohort id + an example request id?

maria: cohort=us-east-prod-canary-10, sample req id=req_abc123. payload is short prompt, seq_len=256.

alex: quick check — auth latency metrics look elevated for the same window, auth_service.latency p95->p99 up 3x. any auth deploys?

jane_support: customer (acme-inc) reported timeouts around 08:05, forwarding logs.

maria: ```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer token_xyz
Content-Type: application/json
{ "input": "Summarize...", "max_tokens": 256 }
```

liam: grab the trace for req_abc123 and check kv cache hit rates. commands:```
rdctl traces get req_abc123 --full
rdctl metrics query "kvcache.hits,kvcache.misses,auth.latency" --start=08:00 --end=08:10
```

sre-bot: alert: canary-p99-threshold triggered for backend pool 'runtime-kernel-v2' (TS 08:07).

alex: initial triage: p95 largely stable, p99 tail correlates with cold KV cache misses on auth token lookup. auth service returned intermittent 503s which cause retries and head-of-line blocking at the runtime host. excerpt: ```
[08:05:12] auth-service: GET /token -> 503 {error: "upstream timeout"}
[08:05:12] runtime-host: auth lookup miss -> synchronous fetch -> increased latency
```

jane_support: confirmed customer tenant 'acme-inc' was routed to canary. they saw ~15% error rate spikes. can we route them back to stable while we investigate?

liam: proposed mitigation: targeted rollback for that tenant + surgical routing away from runtime-kernel-v2. plan: 1) update traffic-split canary 10%->0% for cohort 2) route tenant acme-inc to stable v4.9 3) monitor p99 for 10m. doing step 1 now.

maria: before full rollback, i'd like a quick bisect — two suspects: kernel scheduler change (kernel-v2) vs auth-cache TTL bump. can we run paired canaries to isolate?

alex: good call. repro / bisect plan: spin two 5% canaries: (A) kernel-v2 + old TTL, (B) kernel-v1 + new TTL, run synthetic generator workload matching tenant traffic. commands:```
infra deploy canary --name canary-A --kernel kernel-v2 --auth-ttl 120 --percent 5
infra deploy canary --name canary-B --kernel kernel-v1 --auth-ttl 300 --percent 5
loadgen run --target canary-A,canary-B --profile tenant-acme-synth --duration 10m
```

liam: i'm rolling the traffic split rollback and enabling debug kvcache metrics. will also trigger synthetic load against both canaries.

sre-bot: runbook: if p99 > 300ms after rollback, escalate to runtime-owners and pause all canary ramps.

maria: rollback applied — canary traffic set to 0% for cohort. monitoring... p99 dropped to baseline for acme-inc within ~2 minutes. looks like auth-cache TTL bump was the culprit (cache churn causing backend auth 503s).

alex: root-cause notes: TTL bump increased cache churn and introduced a key-namespace race for tenant-scoped tokens; auth-service saw bursty origin requests and returned 503s under load. action items: 1) revert TTL change in canary config 2) increase kvcache size and warm keys during rollout 3) add circuit-breaker and bulkhead for auth lookup (fail-fast) 4) re-run canary with smaller ramp and synthetic traffic.

jane_support: :thumbsup: i'll notify the customer with timeline & mitigation, offer post-mortem. opening support ticket to close after follow-up.

maria: filing follow-up ticket INC-2026 with summary, root cause, mitigations, and owners. thanks everyone — will schedule a slow canary retest after infra changes.
